scoring_justification: Checker directly identifies resonance peaks in transmission, computes Seebeck spread, and finds maximum ZT from the raw CSV curves, comparing to paper-reported values with tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden reference peaks for C60, Ni@C60, Co@C60; Seebeck spread target; ZT max target
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Extracted from paper: Fig. 2 transmission peak positions, Fig. 3 Seebeck extremes, Fig. 4 ZT max=1.88 at 0.2 eV
hidden_assets.generation_method: Copied directly from the paper's reported values with tolerances chosen to absorb typical DFT+NEGF toolchain spread (different code/parameters).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the authoritative numbers the paper claims; the checker compares the agent's computed curves against them.

outputs.description: Transmission coefficient as a function of energy for bare C60, Ni@C60, and Co@C60. Checker compares resonance peak positions to a hidden reference.
Seebeck coefficient as a function of energy for all three systems. Checker compares range/values near the Fermi level to a hidden reference.
Figure of merit ZT as a function of energy for all three systems. Checker compares maximum ZT value to a hidden reference.

output_contract.notes: Each CSV should contain enough energy points to resolve resonance features in the HOMO-LUMO gap. The energy grid should be fine enough to capture the reported resonance peaks.

steps.description: Extract transmission resonance peaks in the HOMO-LUMO gap and compare with paper-reported positions.
Compute the spread (max-min) of Seebeck coefficient for Co@C60 in the energy window -0.3 to 0 eV and check against paper-reported range.
Find the maximum ZT for Co@C60 in the energy window 0 to 0.3 eV and compare with paper-reported maximum (1.88).
